fixtures.label: Two orders, one organization — the delivery leg
fixtures.description:
The family's FIRST fixture, covering what the family exists for: a CROSS-ORDER sheet. Two orders (964, 1020) under one organization, two destinations, 13 units — no per-order document can express this. Scope `organization:...:all:delivery` pins the `<kind>:<uid>:<gate>:<leg>` grammar (api-cloudrun#824) on its `organization` arm.

1. THE GROUP HEADINGS. Three group dividers across the two orders (`Carts & Ramps`, `Traffic, Safety & Signage`, `Crafty`) — what `buildPackingListForLeg` (core#80, beta.326) exists to keep. The bug it fixed was SILENT: `groupByDestination` strips dividers while `buildPackingList` walks for the last `group` row it passed, so composing them returned null for every heading. The grid rendered and the headings a picker navigates by were absent. Only a rendered sheet catches it.

2. RENTAL AND SALE TOGETHER — the delivery leg's defining property. 964 is three rentals, 1020 a `sale`. Delivery admits both; collection is rental only, because a sale does not come back. A collection-leg fixture is NOT a near-duplicate.

3. A COMPLETE DOCUMENT. `order_count` is 2 and the fold returns 2 with `next_cursor: null`, so `orders.length === order_count` holds — the template REFUSES a short document, and only a fixture satisfying it exercises that.

4. IT PINS AN ABSENCE. All three of 964's bookings carry `shortage: 1` and one carries `stores: []`. The template renders NEITHER, deliberately — a shortage is resolved before the goods leave, not printed on paper that travels with them. An edit that starts printing shortages goes red here rather than reaching a picker.

Deliberately SMALL so the golden reads in one view. The 17-order sheet at `3100 W Fillmore St` is the page-break case and needs its own fixture.

Re-captured 2026-09-06 on the corrected masker (api-cloudrun#837): masked leaves now route by FIELD category, where they were person-name filler. Both orders mask alike because they ARE one destination and the salt is deterministic.

fixtures.label: The collection leg — rental only, components flattened
fixtures.description:
The COLLECTION leg, and the family's first fixture for it: until now roughly half of what this family renders had never been compared against anything, while `visual-diff` reported it passing (templates#226). `PickSheet.leg` is the document's own field, not a render param — the `collection_leg` boolean it was specified with was dropped because the leg split is DATA — so no param state can reach this rendering. Partner: `multi-order-delivery`.

Three load-bearing branches, all unrendered before this: `legKey` selects `packing_list_collection` over `packing_list_delivery`; `legLabel` sets the heading to "Packing List — Collection"; the returns column is driven by `orderHasRentals`.

⭐ RENTAL ONLY, not by chance — the leg's defining property. All nine bookings are `type: rental`, because a sale does not come back; the delivery partner deliberately carries a `sale` line beside its rentals.

⭐ IT PINS TWO INTENDED ABSENCES no other fixture reaches, its source being the only one with real COMPONENTS — five products hang off each of two Pop Up Tent line items, so `path` runs four deep.
1. The sheet does NOT indent them; every row renders flush at one level. The `padding-left` rules in `packing-list.css` are for the three BANNER levels and there is no per-depth row class. A picker wants a flat list, and an edit that starts indenting components goes red here.
2. The same product renders on TWO ROWS rather than consolidating — Tie Down 16 and 40, Milk Crate 2 and 5, Rain Gutter 2 and 5 — because `buildPackingList` keeps its expanded form in depth-first order.

COMPLETE: `order_count` is 1 and the fold returns 1 with `next_cursor: null`, so the `orders.length === order_count` assertion holds.

⭐ Same prod order (1007) as the receipt family's `checkout-no-reference`: that is these tents going out, this is collecting them back.

⚠️ KNOWN ARTIFACT: `scope.name`, `orders[].subject` and `destinations[].name` are masked filler.
